ratings_plot <- ggplot(season_ratings, aes(x = factor(Season), y = AverageRatings)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge", fill = "#faf3b0", color = "#bfa58a") +

       x = "Season",
       y = "Average Ratings") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

Gender Distribution Across Seasons Plot

bakers_summary <- bakers_df %>%
  group_by(Season) %>%
  summarise(TotalContestants = n(), .groups = "drop")

gender_distribution_plot <- ggplot(bakers_df, aes(x = factor(Season), fill = Gender)) +
  geom_bar(position = "stack") +  
  geom_text(data = bakers_summary, 
            aes(x = factor(Season), y = TotalContestants + 0.5, label = TotalContestants), 
            inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 5) +  # Ensure geom_text does not inherit fill
  scale_fill_manual(values = bake_off_colors_gender) +
  labs(title = "Gender Distribution Across Seasons",
       x = "Season",
       y = "Number of Contestants") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        legend.title = element_blank())

gender_distribution_plot

Age Distribution Across Seasons Boxplot

# ChatGPT helped me with the code below to include a different icon to represent the outliers

image_path <- "~/Documents/INSH5302/INSH5302/Data Viz Project 2/whisk.png"

outliers <- bakers_df %>%
  group_by(Season) %>%
  summarise(Q1 = quantile(Age, 0.25),
            Q3 = quantile(Age, 0.75),
            IQR = Q3 - Q1) %>%
  left_join(bakers_df, by = "Season") %>%
  filter(Age < (Q1 - 1.5 * IQR) | Age > (Q3 + 1.5 * IQR)) %>%
  mutate(image = image_path)

age_distribution_plot <- ggplot(bakers_df, aes(x = factor(Season), y = Age)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "#A3CEF1", outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_image(data = outliers, aes(x = factor(Season), y = Age, image = image), 
             size = 0.10, position = position_jitter(width = 0.2)) +  # Increased size & slight jittering
  labs(title = "Age Distribution Across Seasons",
       x = "Season",
       y = "Age") +
  theme_minimal()

age_distribution_plot

Popularity of Themes and Challenges Over the Seasons Plot

# ChatGPT helped me with this code because there are too many themes and I needed to categorize them
episodes_df <- episodes_df %>%
  mutate(ThemeCategory = case_when(
    Theme %in% c("Bread", "Sweet Dough", "Advanced Dough", "Pies", "Pies and Tarts", "Tarts") ~ "Bread & Dough",
    Theme %in% c("Biscuits", "Biscuit", "Biscuits and Traybakes") ~ "Biscuits & Cookies",
    Theme %in% c("Patisserie", "Pâtisserie", "Pastry", "Danish", "Custard") ~ "Pastry & Patisserie",
    Theme %in% c("Cake", "European Cakes", "Festival", "Chocolate", "Caramel") ~ "Cakes",
    Theme %in% c("Dessert", "Desserts", "Pudding", "Dairy") ~ "Desserts & Puddings",
    Theme %in% c("Japanese", "Italian", "German", "Mexican", "Free-from", "Vegan", "Victorian", 
                 "The Roaring Twenties", "Tudor", "The '80s", "Halloween", "Forgotten Bakes") ~ "Cultural & Special Themes",
    TRUE ~ "Creative & Technical Themes"  # Default category
  ))

print(unique(episodes_df$ThemeCategory))
## [1] "Cakes"                       "Biscuits & Cookies"         
## [3] "Bread & Dough"               "Desserts & Puddings"        
## [5] "Pastry & Patisserie"         "Creative & Technical Themes"
## [7] "Cultural & Special Themes"
theme_ratings_treemap_data <- episodes_df %>%
  group_by(Season, ThemeCategory) %>%
  summarise(AverageRating = mean(MyRating..out.of.10., na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")


treemap(theme_ratings_treemap_data,
        index = c("ThemeCategory", "Season"),  # Nest Season inside ThemeCategory
        vSize = "AverageRating",  # Size of each box based on ratings
        type = "index",  # Use categorical colors
        palette = bake_off_colors,  # GBBO Colors
        title = "GBBO Challenge Themes by Ratings",
        fontsize.title = 14,
        fontsize.labels = c(12, 10),  # Larger labels for categories, smaller for seasons
        border.col = "black")  # Black borders for better readability

# Will need the ThemeCategory column for Tableau so I'm downloading a new csv
write.csv(episodes_df, "episodes_data.csv", row.names = FALSE)

Updated Location Data Frame for Location Map in Tableau

# I wanted to use a geographic map in Tableau, so I asked ChatGPT to help me separate the seasons_df dataframe by country and city

unique_locations <- seasons_df %>%
  select(Location) %>%
  mutate(
    City = str_extract(Location, "(?<=,\\s)[^,]+(?=,)"),  # Extract city (middle value)
    Country = word(Location, -1, sep = ",\\s")            # Extract country (last value)
  ) %>%
  select(City, Country) %>%
  distinct()

get_postal_code <- function(city, country, api_key) {
  query <- URLencode(paste(city, country, sep = ", "))
  url <- paste0("https://api.opencagedata.com/geocode/v1/json?q=", query, "&key=", api_key)
  response <- fromJSON(content(GET(url), "text", encoding = "UTF-8"))
  
  if (length(response$results) > 0) {
    components <- response$results[[1]]$components
    return(components$postcode)
  } else {
    return(NA)
  }
}

api_key <- "YOUR_API_KEY"

postal_codes_df <- unique_locations %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(Postal_Code = get_postal_code(City, Country, api_key))

write.csv(postal_codes_df, "Postal_Codes.csv", row.names = FALSE)
